No matter your investing goal, life stage, amount to invest, or know-how, you can invest your way with Schwab.
This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh. The civil rights leader Dolores Huerta has died.
She was a long-time leader of the United Farm Workers' Labor Union. In the '60s and '70s, she led strikes and boycotts to improve working conditions for Mexican-American agricultural workers, and Pierre's Adrian Florido has more.
In the 1960s, Huerta co-founded the union that would become the United Farm Workers with Cesar Chavez. She became a fierce organizer, urging low-paid Mexican-American farmhands to strike for better working conditions.
She was a driving force in the UFW's national boycott of table grapes. It pressured California grape growers to sign the country's first major labor contracts for farm workers.
She left the union in the early 2000s and broadened her activism, training young organizers and advocating for immigrant rights.
Earlier this year, she told the New York Times that decades ago Cesar Chavez had raped her. She said she spoke out in solidarity with other women who'd come forward with credible accounts of child sexual assault by the revered labor activist. Adrian Florido, NPR News.
Ohio and Georgia are the latest midterm election year battlegrounds where voters are hearing today from the most prominent Republican and Democratic Party leaders.
President Trump will attempt to energize the GOP base in Chillicothe. Former President Barack Obama will also work to fire up voters in the Atlanta area. Both are stumping for gubernatorial and congressional candidates in the run-up to the November 3rd vote.
The Fed has just announced it's holding its benchmark interest rates steady. For now, that's what financial markets had expected. Investors believe the central bank will raise rates later this year in an effort to combat stubborn inflation.
President Trump's relationship with Russia's Vladimir Putin is under scrutiny again. We have more on that from NPR's Franco Ordonez.
The administration says Trump is striking deals with Russia, such as buying diesel fuel, to bring economic relief to Americans.
But veteran pollster John McHenry says it's also testing the limits of party loyalty.
Because on the one hand, they don't want to cross or seem to cross President Trump, who's really important to midterm turnout.
But on the other hand, most of them are pretty well established as being against Russia's attacks on Ukraine, against Putin in general.
Now, it's important for the president, any president, to be taking action on the big issues of the day, and that's the cost of living. The problem is gas prices have not really budged as a result.
Franco Ordonez and Pyrenees.
The vast majority of votes cast in Israel's parliamentary elections are counted, but neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's allies nor the opposition bloc has the 61 seat majority needed to determine whether Netanyahu stays or goes.
It is unclear whether the center-right opposition would break campaign pledges and agree to partner with Arab-led parties to secure a majority.
This is NPR News.
There's no indication that Iran has tried to repair or rebuild its nuclear facilities that were damaged by U.S. and Israeli military strikes. NPR's Hadil al-Shalchi reports.
The international atomic energy chief, Rafael Grossi, said the U.N. has been unable to verify the status of Iran's uranium stockpile and urged Iran to give inspectors access.
He said that despite the lack of on-the-ground monitors, there was still no evidence that Iran was trying to repair or reconstruct the nuclear sites damaged in recent U.S.-Israeli strikes.
President Trump has said that one of his main reasons for going to war with Iran was to eliminate their capability to develop a nuclear weapon.
Hadil al-Shalchi, NPR News, Istanbul.
A leading market research firm says many Canadian tourists are still snubbing the U.S. in part because of politics. In Paris, Kirk Sigler says rural towns and border states are feeling the financial pinch.
The major drops that were traced back to Trump first suggesting Canada become the 51st state have stirred anxiety in rural border states like Vermont, Idaho, and Montana, where Canadians have historically traveled to shop and vacation.
The ski resort town of Whitefish, Montana, by Glacier National Park, has historically relied on Canada for about a quarter of its business but has seen a precipitous drop in numbers since Trump returned to office.
That's Kirk Sigler reporting. It's NPR News.
